chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said:

Abu Hanifa exited from the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) was standing, and he (peace be upon him) was a young boy. So Abu Hanifa said to him (peace be upon him), 'O boy! Where can the strangers in your city place (their faeces and urine)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They should keep away from the courtyards of the Masjids, and banks of the rivers, and the places where the fruits fall from the trees, and the houses (places) of combat, and he should neither face the Qiblah by defecation nor urination, and should raise his clothes, and place it where he so desires to'.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) teach about where to relieve oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the early intellectual prowess of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), who, as a young boy, engaged the prominent Sunni jurist Abu Hanifa with precise rulings on ritual purity (fiqh al-najāsah). The Imam’s response not only outlines specific locations to avoid for privacy and cleanliness—such as mosques, rivers, and fruit trees—but also establishes the fundamental etiquette of not facing or turning one's back to the Qiblah during excretion, a practice rooted in Quranic reverence for the direction of prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, raising it, said,

‘Abu Haneefa exited from the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> was standing, and he<sup>asws</sup> was a young boy. So Abu Haneefa said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O boy! Where can the strangers in your<sup>asws</sup> city place (their faeces and urine)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should keep away from the courtyards of the Masjids, and banks of the rivers, and the places where the fruits fall from the trees, and the houses (places) of combat, and he should neither face the Qiblah by defecation nor urination, and should raise his clothes, and place it where he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated in a marfu‘ manner the following: “

Once, abu Hanifah came out of a meeting with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Abu al-Hassan, Musa, a young boy at that time, was standing in the meeting place. Abu Hanifah asked him, ‘O young man, where does an outsider relieve himself of nature’s demand in your town?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘You must avoid the courtyard of a Masjid, banks of canals, places where fruits fall from trees and people’s rest areas. Do not face the direction of al-Ka‘bah, when defecating or urinating and keep your clothes away (from pollution). Thereafter relieve yourself wherever you like.’”
